title: Order placed
sub: MRI lumbar spine, in the chart

d.what: The clinician selects the study. Nothing has been committed and nobody has yet asked whether authorisation is needed — historically this is the step where the whole process stalls.
The EHR posts the draft order, patient and coverage to the CDS service. Prefetch has already resolved the patient and coverage, so no callback is needed.
d.fail: If the service does not answer inside roughly 5 seconds the EHR drops the card and the clinician sees nothing. Budget accordingly.

d.what: The question that never had an API before. CRD answers covered / not covered, authorisation required or not, and which documents will be wanted.
d.fail: CRD unreachable or coverage stale → a card saying so, and a case flagged for manual eligibility. Never assume 'not required'.

title: Case opened
sub: Written to the platform, event emitted

d.what: A case row, an event on the bus, and an audit entry. Every later step subscribes to this event rather than polling.
d.fail: None — this is a local write.

title: Eligibility & benefits
sub: Coverage active on the date of service?

d.what: Confirms the plan is active, resolves the benefit tier and member cost share, and re-confirms the authorisation requirement against the specific place of service.
d.fail: Terminated coverage or a member-not-found response escalates immediately — everything downstream is wasted work otherwise.

title: Evidence gathering
sub: Find what the criteria will be judged on

d.what: Queries the repository across every connected source, expands the payer's document list into searchable value sets, and records what it looked for and did not find.
proto: TEFCA when the record is elsewhere
d.fail: A missing document is reported as a gap with the exact query that failed. It never substitutes a weaker document silently.

d.what: The reason evidence gathering is a query and not an integration project. The repository holds the reconciled longitudinal record; terminology turns 'TB screen' into a LOINC value set.
d.fail: An unreconciled duplicate patient record is the dangerous failure here — which is why identity resolution sits in the platform, not the workflow.

title: Criteria check
sub: Per criterion: met, partial or gap

d.what: Walks the payer's criteria one at a time and attaches the specific line of the specific document that satisfies each. Anything met only by inference is downgraded.
d.fail: Low confidence or a partial match does not block the packet — it flags it, and the flag is what the human reads first.

d.what: Fetches the payer's questionnaire and fills every answer the repository already holds. What cannot be autofilled is left visibly empty, never guessed.
d.fail: An autofilled answer without provenance is treated as not autofilled.

d.who: Pre-auth coordinator, or a clinician for clinical assertions
d.what: The hard gate. The reviewer sees each criterion, the evidence behind it, the confidence, and every gap. They can edit, add evidence, or reject. Nothing is submitted without this.
proto: Signed approval written to the audit log
d.fail: This step is deliberately not automatable. Thresholds decide how much is pre-filled, never whether a human is involved.

d.what: Sends on whatever transport the payer supports and records the tracking number. Three payer tiers, one interface upward.
d.fail: Transport failure retries with backoff, then escalates. SLA breaches escalate on the clock, not only on error.

d.what: Clean packets against a full Da Vinci payer can auto-adjudicate in minutes. Specialty drugs and surgery route to a human reviewer. Legacy payers take days.
d.fail: An unparseable response escalates rather than being retried blindly.

d.what: The authorisation number is written to the case and pushed back to the EHR order, scheduling is released, and the patient is told in plain language.
d.fail: An authorisation that exists in your system but not on the order is an authorisation that will be re-requested.

d.who: Submission & Tracking Agent, then Clinical Evidence Agent
d.what: The pend reason is parsed into a specific, named missing item. The evidence agent re-queries, including sources it did not search the first time. If the record genuinely does not exist, it says so and asks a human to obtain it.
proto: Event bus — a new lab landing wakes the case on its own
d.fail: This is the loop that quietly eats staff hours today. The event bus is what makes it cheap: nobody has to remember to check.

d.what: Reads the reason code and the criterion the payer cited, re-queries for what would have answered it, and drafts a letter citing policy section and evidence by date and source.
d.fail: The letter is always a draft. The agent never files on its own authority.

d.what: A clinical assertion is being made to a payer over a clinician's name. A coordinator cannot approve this one; the thresholds do not apply.
proto: Signed approval, attributed, in the audit log

d.what: Re-adjudication, frequently with a peer-to-peer call. The agent prepares the briefing sheet the physician takes into that call.
d.fail: Appeal deadlines are hard. The tracker is the only thing standing between a viable appeal and a missed window.
